newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BRITAIN CALLS FOR "FRIENDLY RIVALRY" IN WORLD CUP ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRITAIN CALLS FOR "FRIENDLY RIVALRY" IN WORLD CUP ROW.

text.p: Britain's sports minister on Tuesday described UEFA's backing for Germany to host the 2006 World Cup as "difficult to understand" but said he hoped England would be allowed to compete for the honour in friendly rivalry.

In answer to a parliamentary question, Iain Sproat said he met representatives of the English Football Association (F.A.) on Monday to discuss the refusal by UEFA (Europe's governing body) to consider an English bid.

The F.A. have said they were astounded to receive a fax from UEFA on January 31 which said a meeting of its committee had "recalled that it had already committed itself to supporting the candidature of the German F.A. as organiser of the World Cup in 2006".
"From the information presented to us, we find it difficult to understand UEFA's position," Sproat said.
However, he noted the decision was a matter for the world body, FIFA, who had indicated they would not be influenced by UEFA's position.
"I have written today to my opposite number in Germany to express my hope that our bids can be conducted in a spirit of friendly rivalry," Sproat said.
